modelResponse.episodeSummary: 70yo male, sinus bradycardia, moderate severity, hemodynamically stable but symptomatic
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Digoxin Toxicity precipitated by Amiodarone-induced drug-drug interaction
modelResponse.mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein (P-gp), the primary efflux transporter for digoxin, leading to decreased renal and biliary clearance of digoxin and subsequent elevation of serum levels to toxic concentrations.
contributingFactors: Failure to adjust digoxin dose upon initiation of amiodarone loading
Concurrent amiodarone and simvastatin use (contributing to muscle aches/CK 1200 U/L HIGH via CYP3A4 inhibition)
Amiodarone-induced potentiation of warfarin (INR 5.8 CRITICAL HIGH)

rejectedAlternatives.why: potassium: 4.0 mmol/L is within normal reference range (3.5-5.1)
troponinT 0.02 ng/mL is only mildly high and not consistent with acute ischemia; no ST elevation noted
tsh: 2.1 mIU/L is within normal reference range (0.4-4.0)

recommendedActions: STOP Simvastatin immediately (due to CK 1200 U/L HIGH and amiodarone interaction)
HOLD Warfarin until INR is corrected
Administer Digoxin-specific antibody fragments (DigiFab) given digoxinLevel 2.4 ng/mL TOXIC and symptomatic bradycardia
Monitor potassium and magnesium levels closely
